# JSDoc

The source of truth is the JSDoc block in the file; `npm run lint:js` requires it. For what is handled where see `HANDLERS.md`.

## app/products/webapp/ext/fragment/DetailsForm.js

Module of the custom section "Details" (ADR-0027 decision 5 and its amendment "Browser proof of the
fragment"): a factory builds one form element per detail row of the product by the attribute's value
type; the fragment names no attribute. Rows come from the server in `position` order (no client sorter).

without rows carries `details: []`, the server's `after('EDIT')` fill comes later. Since the rows binding

### syncFormElements

`function syncFormElements(root)` (line 1030)

Aligns the form elements with the row contexts of the `details` binding (PLAN R2-D2): the element of a
row that stays is kept with its controls, its focus, its own `selections` binding and its list message;
a new row gets a new element, a row that is gone loses its element, and the order follows the server's
`position` order. A list binding with a factory would destroy and rebuild every element on each change
of the binding (`ManagedObject#updateAggregation` without extended change detection).

| Tag | Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| @param | root | `sap.m.VBox` | the fragment root |

### clearFormElements

`function clearFormElements(root)` (line 1070)

Destroys every form element when the `details` collection is refreshed (its `refresh` event: the
`#SubcategoryChanged` side effect, the Edit re-read of ruling B2, a new product context). The event
fires inside the binding's reset, before the model refreshes the dependent bindings of the old rows;
destroyed bindings are skipped there, so a row the server has just deleted sends no `GET` of its
`selections` or values (a 404 would open an error dialog). The following `change` builds the rows again.

| Tag | Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| @param | root | `sap.m.VBox` | the fragment root |

## srv/catalog-service.js

### CatalogService

`export default class CatalogService extends cds.ApplicationService` (line 20)

Handlers of CatalogService.
- READ Permissions: tells the Fiori UI whether the caller may edit. Enforcement is declarative
  (`@requires` / `@restrict` in catalog-service.cds); this is the signal behind UI.CreateHidden /
  UI.UpdateHidden / UI.DeleteHidden (ADR-0013).
- importProducts: creates active products from an xlsx workbook, all-or-nothing (ADR-0021).
- PATCH Products.drafts: clears a subcategory that does not belong to the new category
  (ADR-0024 decision 3); the pair itself is checked by the `@assert` constraint (decision 2).
  Then a new subcategory reconciles the detail rows of the draft (ADR-0027 decision 3).
- EDIT Products: fills the detail rows a product without rows lacks (ADR-0027 decision 3, PLAN D13).

### resetStaleSubcategory

`async function resetStaleSubcategory(Subcategories, req)` (line 54)

Dependent field reset on a draft (ADR-0024 decision 3): when a draft PATCH changes the category
without carrying the subcategory, a stored subcategory that does not belong to the new category
is cleared, so the stale value neither stays visible nor fails at Save. A subcategory of the new
category is kept (for example one chosen before the category on a new draft). Silent: no message,
no rejection; active writes are not reset, there the `@assert` constraint rejects (decision 2).

Rows generated from the assignment on a draft (ADR-0027 decision 3, U2, U3): a draft PATCH that

### reconcileDetailRows

`async function reconcileDetailRows(srv, draft, subcategory, req)` (line 115)

After the call the draft holds exactly one row per attribute assigned to the subcategory, the
common ones unchanged (ADR-0027 decision 3): rows of assigned attributes keep their values and
selections and get the assignment's position; the other rows are deleted (their draft selections
go with them, research R8); each missing attribute gets an empty row. Rows are written to the
draft table directly, so they carry the parent's DraftAdministrativeData_DraftUUID (research
R10: the insert fails without it). When deleted rows held a value, the warning
PRODUCTS_DETAILS_VALUES_REMOVED goes to the response (PLAN D16).

### unzippedSize

`export function unzippedSize(bytes, limit)` (line 179)

Count the unpacked bytes of a zip archive without keeping them, so that a small upload cannot
unpack into gigabytes inside the parser (ADR-0021 amendment D). The walk follows the records in
the order the streaming reader of read-excel-file reads them, not the central directory it
ignores (research 8.3, 8.4):
- local file headers from offset 0; the entry data runs for the compressed size of the header,
  or, when flag bit 3 is set and that size is 0, up to the data-descriptor signature, followed
  by the 16 descriptor bytes;
- central-directory records are skipped by their lengths;
- the walk stops at the end record, or at the first unknown record after the central directory.
Every entry is inflated with `maxOutputLength` set to the remaining budget, so the function's own
memory never exceeds `limit`; a stored entry counts its length.

| Tag | Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| @param | bytes | `Buffer` | zip archive |
| @param | limit | `number` | budget of unpacked bytes for the whole archive |
| @returns |  | `{ size: number } \| { error: 'TOO_LARGE' \| 'INVALID' }` | the unpacked size; `TOO_LARGE` for a declared size above the remaining budget (the reader allocates it), a zip64 size marker, or inflated bytes above the budget; `INVALID` for an unreadable record (unknown signature before the central directory, truncated header, missing data descriptor, zlib data error). Empty input gives `{ size: 0 }`. |
